title: Crisp Onion, Potato and Spinach Pakora with Green Chutney
summary: Sliced onion, grated potato and spinach are tossed with spices and salt, squeezed to release their juice, bound with besan and cornflour and fried at 185 °C.
equipment: deep heavy pan or Dutch oven

ingredients.item: large red onion, halved and thinly sliced
floury potato, peeled and coarsely grated
Kashmiri chilli powder (pure chilli) or paprika
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: plus a few drops if needed

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Season the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the vegetables with the chilli, spices and salt and squeeze for 45 seconds until they soften.

steps.title: Bind
steps.text: Stir in the besan, cornflour and baking powder, then just enough water to make a sticky mass.

steps.title: Make the chutney
steps.text: Blend the coriander, mint, chilli, lime, sugar, salt and water.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry heaped spoonfuls, 5 at a time, for 1.5-2 minutes a side until deep golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drain and serve hot with the chutney.

tips: Squeezing the vegetables makes a batter that needs very little water.
Let the oil recover between batches for crisp, not greasy, pakora.
Keep batches warm on a rack in a low oven.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best fried and eaten the same day. Cool leftovers, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, re-crisped in a 200 °C oven for 6-8 minutes until piping hot.
